chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The zakat of jewelry is that it be lent out.

key_terms.أَنْ يُعَارَ: That it be lent out, referring to the specific act of lending the jewelry as the means of fulfilling the zakat obligation.
key_terms.الْحُلِيِّ: Jewelry, specifically referring to gold and silver ornaments worn by humans.
key_terms.زَكَاةُ: Purification or alms-tax, referring to the obligatory charity in Islam.

ai.seo_question: What is the method for paying zakat on gold jewelry according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that the purification of jewelry (*huliy*) is achieved by lending it out. This view, primarily associated with the Ja'fari school, interprets 'lending' as a mechanism for circulating wealth to the needy, thereby fulfilling the spiritual and material obligation of zakat without necessarily selling the items. It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding movable assets, distinguishing it from the more common practice of selling jewelry to pay the due amount.
